about: Outside records about a seller: company registers, chambers of commerce, trade fairs, sanctions lists and website traffic. Used to look a seller up outside the page it sells on, in marketplace scans and website checks.
how_to_change: Each country has its own file next to this one (china.json, usa.json...). Safely reads the seller's country from the page and runs global.json plus that country's file. A country with no file gets global.json only.
sources: the outside records Safely will read. status 'planned' means not built yet; 'live' means Safely reads it now.
access: 'offline' (checked inside Safely, no internet), 'api' (free official API), 'download' (a public list file), 'scrape' (read the website), 'paid_api'.
cost: 'free', 'small_fee' or 'paid'. key_env: the name of the key in .env on the server (the key itself is never written here).
step: the build step that adds the source (see claude/databases-plan.md in the Safely project).
cards: same as b2b.json (warning_points, points_when_value, enabled). Every database card has group 'outside_records', so the extension and dashboard can show them in their own section.

Found = a good sign. Not found = NOT a warning: a 'Not found' card (information only, no points) when the check really ran, no card when a site did not answer. Only a false claim (fake company number, fake fair) or a sanctions match is a warning.

sources.name: Sanctions lists (US OFAC, UN)
sources.what_it_does: Is the company on a US or UN banned list? Downloaded once a day; only companies, whole names.

sources.name: EU sanctions list
sources.what_it_does: Is the company on the EU banned list? Downloaded once a day with the US and UN lists (same switch, SANCTIONS_CHECK_ENABLED); only companies, whole names.

sources.name: GLEIF (LEI register)
sources.what_it_does: Official world register of company IDs (LEI). Bigger companies only. Searched by the whole company name; needs GLEIF_CHECK_ENABLED=true.

sources.name: Wayback Machine
sources.what_it_does: Since when the website has been saved by the Wayback Machine. Card "Website history"; needs WEBSITE_RECORDS_CHECK_ENABLED=true.

sources.name: Tranco list
sources.what_it_does: Is the website among the 1 million most visited websites? Card "Website traffic"; needs WEBSITE_RECORDS_CHECK_ENABLED=true.

sources.name: crt.sh
sources.what_it_does: When the website got its first security certificate. Card "Security certificate"; needs WEBSITE_RECORDS_CHECK_ENABLED=true.

sources.name: OpenCorporates
sources.what_it_does: Company registers of many countries in one place.

sources.name: Shipping records (Panjiva, ImportGenius)
sources.what_it_does: Does the company really ship goods?

cards.what_it_checks: Whether a company with exactly the seller's name is on the US (OFAC), UN or EU sanctions lists. A match is a warning (it may be another company with the same name); no match is a good sign but says nothing more. Needs SANCTIONS_CHECK_ENABLED=true in .env.

Whether a company with exactly the seller's name is in the official GLEIF register (LEI). Registered in the seller's country is a good sign; listed as closed is a warning; the same name in another country, or not in the register, is information only and never adds to the score. Needs GLEIF_CHECK_ENABLED=true in .env.

Whether the company number the supplier gives (China's 18-character code, Brazil's CNPJ, France's SIREN / SIRET / VAT number) is a real number: its check digits must add up. Checked inside Safely, no internet. A number that fails is a warning (made up or mistyped).

What the country's own register says about the company number (Brazil: Receita Federal via BrasilAPI; France: recherche-entreprises.api.gouv.fr, and INSEE's Sirene API when that does not answer and INSEE_API_KEY is set). Active under the same name is a good sign; another company's name is a warning; closed is a warning; not found is information only. Needs REGISTERS_CHECK_ENABLED=true in .env.

Whether the EU VAT number the supplier gives (any EU country, written with its country code: FR..., DE..., IT...) is active in the EU's VIES register (free, no key). Active under the seller's name is a good sign; active under another company's name is a warning; not active is a smaller warning (VIES only lists numbers that may trade with other EU countries). Some countries never give the name. Needs REGISTERS_CHECK_ENABLED=true in .env.

Whether a company with exactly the seller's name is listed on the US stock market (SEC EDGAR's list of listed companies, downloaded once a day; free, no key). 'Listed company' is a good sign; 'Not on the stock market' is information only and is shown only for US sellers. Needs REGISTERS_CHECK_ENABLED=true and SEC_CONTACT_EMAIL in .env (the SEC asks for a contact email).

For US sellers only: whether a company with exactly the seller's name (legal or trade name) is registered with the US government in SAM.gov. Active is a good sign; excluded by the US government (barred from government work) is a warning; expired or not registered is information only. A basic key allows 10 lookups a day, so each answer is kept for 7 days and at most SAM_GOV_DAILY_LIMIT (10 when not set) lookups are made a day. Needs REGISTERS_CHECK_ENABLED=true and SAM_GOV_API_KEY in .env (the key expires after about 90 days).

Whether a company with exactly the seller's name is a member of a chamber of commerce whose member pages are public: the Hong Kong General Chamber of Commerce (HKGCC, for Hong Kong and China sellers) or the thousands of local chambers on ChamberMaster / GrowthZone (for US sellers and sellers with no country file). One Google search (Serper) finds the member page, which is then opened to read the name. A member is a good sign; a member whose website differs from the seller's is information only (maybe another company with the same name); not a member is 'Not found' (information only, never a warning; no card when a member page could not be opened). Needs CHAMBERS_CHECK_ENABLED=true and SERPER_API_KEY in .env. Only searched for US and Canada sellers (ChamberMaster) and China / Hong Kong sellers (HKGCC); for every other country, or when the page gives no country, nothing is searched and the card says 'Not checked' (information only).

Whether a company with exactly the seller's name is an exhibitor at the current Canton Fair session (the fair's own exhibitor search, as 365.cantonfair.org.cn uses it; free, no key). Asked for China and Hong Kong sellers, and for any seller that says 'Canton Fair' about itself. An exhibitor is a good sign (shows session, phase, section and booth). A seller that claims the fair but is not in this session's list is a warning; otherwise not an exhibitor is 'Not found' (information only). Needs TRADE_SHOWS_CHECK_ENABLED=true in .env.

Whether the seller, found as a Canton Fair exhibitor (same whole-name match as the 'Canton Fair' card), is certified by China Customs as an AEO (Advanced Certified Enterprise): the fair's own exhibitor data marks it (isAeo 'Y' or an 'AEO' badge). China Customs' own lookup (credit.customs.gov.cn) refuses visitors outside mainland China, so it is not asked. Certified is a good sign; otherwise no card. Needs TRADE_SHOWS_CHECK_ENABLED=true in .env.

Whether a company with exactly the seller's name is an exhibitor at the HKTDC fairs Safely reads (HKTDC_FAIRS in trade_shows.rs; now the Hong Kong Electronics Fair, Spring Edition). Each fair's exhibitor search page is opened with the name and its data read: booth, and the HKTDC fairs the company exhibited at in recent years. Asked for China and Hong Kong sellers. An exhibitor is a good sign; not found is 'Not found' (information only - HKTDC runs many fairs, so it is never a warning). Needs TRADE_SHOWS_CHECK_ENABLED=true in .env.

Whether a company with exactly the seller's name is an exhibitor at the US fairs on Map Your Show that Safely reads (MYS_SHOWS in trade_shows.rs; now CES). The show's own exhibitor search (ajax/remote-proxy.cfm?action=search) is asked with the name. Asked for every seller. An exhibitor is a good sign (show, year, booths, link); not found is 'Not found' (information only), shown to US sellers only. Needs TRADE_SHOWS_CHECK_ENABLED=true in .env.

Whether a company with exactly the seller's name is an exhibitor at the Brazil fairs Safely reads (in trade_shows.rs): on Informa's Swapcard platform (SWAPCARD_FAIRS: Hospitalar 2027, Fispal Tecnologia 2026, Fispal Food Service 2026 - each whole list read once a day) and on RX's Algolia search (ALGOLIA_FAIRS: Feicon 2027 - one search per scan, with the public search key the fair's page gives every visitor). Asked for every seller. An exhibitor is a good sign (fair, booth, link to the list); not found is one 'Not found' card naming every Brazil fair searched (information only), shown to Brazil sellers only. Needs TRADE_SHOWS_CHECK_ENABLED=true in .env.

Whether a company with exactly the seller's name (Maison&Objet: the company or its brand) is an exhibitor at the French fairs Safely reads (ALGOLIA_FAIRS in trade_shows.rs; now SIAL Paris 2026 and Maison&Objet Paris, searched on Algolia with the public search key the fair's page gives every visitor). One search per scan. Asked for every seller. An exhibitor is a good sign (fair, stand, link to its exhibitor page); not found is one 'Not found' card naming every French fair searched (information only), shown to France sellers only. Needs TRADE_SHOWS_CHECK_ENABLED=true in .env.

Shown when Safely reads no trade fair lists for the seller's country (only China/Hong Kong, the USA, Brazil and France have them): 'Not checked', information only, never a warning and no points. It says so plainly and adds how many fairs in other countries were looked at without finding the name. Not shown when a fair in another country lists the seller (that fair's own card shows instead). Needs TRADE_SHOWS_CHECK_ENABLED=true in .env.

The seller's reputation on Reclame Aqui, Brazil's biggest complaint site. One Google search (Serper) finds the company's page (reclameaqui.com.br/empresa/...), which is read through ScraperAPI from a Brazilian address (the site refuses many other countries); the grade, score, complaints and answered/solved rates are in the page's own tags. The page counts only when its CNPJ is the seller's, or (no CNPJ given) its whole name is the seller's. 'Não recomendada' is a warning, 'Ruim' a smaller one; 'Regular' or no grade yet is information only; 'Bom', 'Ótimo' and 'RA1000' are good signs; not on Reclame Aqui is 'Not found' (information only; no card when a page could not be read). Asked for Brazil sellers and any seller that gives a CNPJ; answers kept 7 days. Needs RECLAME_AQUI_CHECK_ENABLED=true, SERPER_API_KEY and SCRAPERAPI_KEY in .env.

The seller's rating (A+ to F) and accreditation at the Better Business Bureau. BBB's search page (bbb.org/search?find_text={name}&find_country=USA) carries its results as data in the page (__PRELOADED_STATE__); it is read through ScraperAPI from the USA (BBB blocks many visitors with a robot check). A business counts only when its whole name is the seller's. F is a warning, D a smaller one; A+ to A- a good sign; B, C or not rated information only; not on BBB is 'Not found' (information only). Asked for US sellers; answers kept 7 days. Needs BBB_CHECK_ENABLED=true and SCRAPERAPI_KEY in .env.

Since when the Wayback Machine (web.archive.org) has saved the seller's own website. Saved over a year ago is a good sign; newer or never saved is information only and never adds to the score (a brand-new domain is already warned about by 'Website age'). Needs WEBSITE_RECORDS_CHECK_ENABLED=true in .env.

Whether the seller's own website is among the world's 1 million most visited websites (Tranco list). In the list is a good sign; not in it is information only (normal for small companies). Needs WEBSITE_RECORDS_CHECK_ENABLED=true in .env.

When the seller's own website got its first security certificate (crt.sh, the public log of certificates). Over a year ago is a good sign; recent or none found is information only. Needs WEBSITE_RECORDS_CHECK_ENABLED=true in .env.
